title: What Linear Algebra Studies — Fundamentals of Linear Algebra
description: This entry covers What Linear Algebra Studies as part of the fundamentals of linear algebra. In this field, vectors matters because directed quantities with magnitude and direction, added componentwise and scaled. It is taught at the Foundations level of the teaching ladder, building from first principles toward professional practice, with each concept defined before it is used.
overview: Linear Algebra is the field concerned with Vectors, matrices, and linear transformations: the language of data, graphics, and quantum mechanics. What Linear Algebra Studies belongs to its essential core. Concretely: Vectors — directed quantities with magnitude and direction, added componentwise and scaled. And Vector spaces — sets closed under addition and scaling, with bases and dimension. Mastering this entry means being able to explain the topic in plain sentences, recognize it in real cases, and apply it alongside the neighboring ideas of the Foundations tier.
core_concepts: Vectors: directed quantities with magnitude and direction, added componentwise and scaled.
Vector spaces: sets closed under addition and scaling, with bases and dimension.
key_laws: Rank-nullity theorem: rank plus nullity equals the number of columns.
vocabulary: Basis: a minimal spanning set, the coordinate system of a vector space.
Kernel: the inputs a transformation sends to zero.
methods: Gaussian elimination: systematic row operations reducing systems to triangular form.
history: Linear algebra grew from 19th-century determinants and Cayley's matrices, matured with vector spaces in the early 1900s, and became the indispensable computational language of the computer era, from graphics to machine learning.
